body: If the tag name is longer than maximum size, the remove button does not appear (probably gets clipped). Deleting a tag moves the project higher in the list: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c122e48-5830-4c04-b91d-d56539731d22 That's because deleting a tag modifies `project.godot` and affects modification date of the project. It's the reason why tag editing is done via the dialog. No matter how many tags you add or remove, the project file is updated only once the dialog is closed. Also the deleting could have some confirmation. You can't undo it and it might be easy to missclick on small tags.
Yeah, I'll work on those.

@KoBeWi I'm thinking, would it be a problem to move tags into the projects.cfg file? When adding a new project it's populated with the tags in the project.godot file, but that project is also migrated to the projects.cfg, so it wouldn't be hard to also migrate its tags as well. This will prevent the editing issue.

As for the dialog, maybe it can also have the option to never show again, but it will need a place to be reshown if the user changes their mind.

> I'm thinking, would it be a problem to move tags into the projects.cfg file?

Then the tags wouldn't be part of the project. If the project is shared (in a team, between different computers, or open-source), the tags wouldn't carry over.

> Then the tags wouldn't be part of the project. If the project is shared (in a team, between different computers, or open-source), the tags wouldn't carry over.

@KoBeWi  Okay, so this can be solved in two ways. The first is that the Project Manager instantiates the tags from the `projects.cfg`, but the tags remain in the `project.godot` as a "reference" so when it gets passed along and added to someone's project list, the tags can be migrated from there into the section of that project in the `projects.cfg`

The second solution would be to have a `.tags` file in every project and the tags get read from there.

Edit: The `.tags` file will be prone to merge conflicts, that really only leaves the first option.
Edit 2: On further thought, the above doesn't really apply so much as the `project.godot` file would also cause similar merge conflicts in the scenario I was thinking about. Going forward with the `.tags` implementation for now.

Found an issue with button, the text does not respect its maximum size, so although the text is no longer rendered and the button doesn't grow, everything else acts as though the text is still physically there, creating that empty space. This is solved using a label with clip_text on or with text_overrun_behavior set. Edit: Solved in the PR by using NOTIFICATION_READY to get the button size and force that to be its minimum. Edit 2: Solution moved to different PR as temporary supplemental fix.

I've run into an issue, I managed to get the tags to work properly without changing the list, and for compatibility, those tags will be written to the `project.godot` file on project manager close, however, because no changes are being made while the project manager is open, if a tag is changed on an old project, the project version will change when the project manager is opened, which may catch some users by surprise. There are two ways to go about this:

1. Leave it as is
2. Create a new `save_custom` function in project_settings.cpp. It will be called `save_custom_no_feature` and won't update the `config\features` parameter.

> There are two ways to go about this:
Leave it as is

This problem existed before this PR, so it can be left as is.

I haven't yet added the "confirm tag delete" as I'm not sure where to put the setting to turn in back on, and I don't want to have the dialog without a "don't show again" checkbox or a way to reverse said option.

25/06 Edit: As a compromise for the warning popup, the remove button icon will turn red when hovered. This is achieved by using a new icon which will be reused in a later PR.

@Calinou implemented all feedback. As for the red modulate, it was a compromise because KoBeWi wanted a dialog prompt when pressing the button to remove the tag 

> Also the deleting could have some confirmation. You can't undo it and it might be easy to missclick on small tags.

The button and tags seem to be misaligned. > 25/06 Edit: As a compromise for the warning popup, the remove button icon will turn red when hovered. That doesn't really help. Red icon can still be missclicked 🙃 Instead of "Don't show again" option, the dialog could have "Hold Shift to skip this dialog". > The second solution would be to have a .tags file in every project and the tags get read from there. Sorry for not replying earlier, but the .tags file isn't really a good idea. It clutters the main project directory and users will be unhappy with that. The simplest solution for the problem is always using the original modified time from when the project was first added to the list. This way modifying tags or renaming the project won't affect sorting. > When clicking a tag in the Manage Project Tags dialog, it's not removed from the project (you need click on the X button next to it instead): This one is not addressed.

@KoBeWi 

> Instead of "Don't show again" option, the dialog could have "Hold Shift to skip this dialog".

I added the setting as `project_manager/show_warning_on_tag_deletion`. It is on by default but can now be turned off with the "Don't Show Again" checkbox.

> The button and tags seem to be misaligned.

@Calinou wanted the tag and add button to be the same size, the misalignment is most likely because they are in different sections. The tags are in the `tag_container` while the add button is in the `title_hb` (same as the `tag_container`). The only two options would be to:

1.  leave it misaligned 
2. revert it back to the tags being larger.

I personally prefer option two as it breaks it up visually.

> The simplest solution for the problem is always using the original modified time from when the project was first added to the list. This way modifying tags or renaming the project won't affect sorting.

Looked into this and the `_sort_projects()` is a bit confusing so I don't know how to work with it atm. My current solution is to simply make the .tags file temporary, it is created when the project manager is opened and deleted when the project manager is closed. It can also be added to the `.gitignore` list if need be.

Also fixed the last issue.
I opened a separate PR for the time sorting: #121043

In terms of UX, this seems fine at a glance, but I have two remaining questions:

- What should we do with the **Manage Tags** button on the right? The "+" button on each project achieves the same purpose now.
- Is it a problem to show the delete tag buttons at all times for all projects? It looks a bit noisy to me.

@godotengine/usability Any thoughts on this?

For reference, it looks like this now:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c385b5a8-c641-42c6-8864-6c574b72f5af
Maybe show the X only on mouse hover? I recall seeing this in other software.
I agree that the `X` makes it super noisy (and kinda' ugly). Perhaps we can move the 'delete tag' option to the context menu which can be opened using RMB on desktop and with a long press on mobile?

@Calinou I made it so the remove button only shows when hovering over the project. Can add also add a timer if deemed necessary.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/146adf99-2fe7-443b-84e7-87ac0ba9b3a3
The jumpy behavior as a result of these appearing and disappearing `X` buttons is a big no-no in terms of readability and usability 🫣

You should hide the X button, but not remove it entirely so that it doesn't cause reflows. This can be done by using `set_modulate(Color(1, 1, 1, 0))` on the button icon, instead of using `hide()` or `set_visible(false)`.

@Calinou there was no way to set it on the button icon itself, and setting the button to be transparent left ugly gaps. The only other solution was to remove the icon. Which looks like this: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85f24719-6a77-40da-8378-5e9d36998180 This in my opinion looks a bit ugly as well as there is a lot of negative space. A possible solution could be to transfer over the color of the rects to the button so the negative space has some usage Example: (this looks extra ugly because its just a dirty mockup) I feel like the image above would be easier to get used to than the negative space of the missing icon. As for @AdriaandeJongh suggestion, the tags mouse filter is set to passthrough so that the project can be selected behind it and RMB already opens the project's context menu. If there is a way around that that isn't too complicated, I can give it a go.

I personally, genuinely do not see the benefit of adding the remove button after every tag. Removing tags on the fly is a comparatively uncommon operation that is better performed in the current "Manage Project Tags" dialog.

I think we need a consensus here. "Damned if you do, and damned if you don't". Because having the remove button would mean that *either*:
- individuals tags would jump around in size, which is extremely uncomfortable.
- the size of every tag would be expanded to accomodate a button that is not always there, which, doesn't matter how it's done, is way too much space to dedicate to tags.

But not having the remove button would destroy most of this PR.

If I have to suggest, perhaps there is a way out: When a label is hovered, **shrink** the tag's label by the width of the remove button, then add the remove button inside the tag.
If you cannot implement this, I would suggest removing the feature outright _in my opinion_.

The tag button itself cannot get any smaller without clipping the text as I've already removed as much space as I could to accommodate the remove button. If you look at Calinou's video, a lot the tags are repeating, Official and Demo in particular,  that is a good case for categories, or at the least a directory specific project list, it reduces the amount of tags needed per project, which in turn reduces the "noise" of the close button.

> When a label is hovered, shrink the tag's label by the width of the remove button, then add the remove button inside the tag.

Or maybe the button could overlap the label? Like, it could be a child of the label, anchored to right center. Then it could be also hidden with visibility instead of modulate.
The current implementation, or the one I suggested where the remove button uses the tag color are the only two viable implementations of this feature

> Or maybe the button could overlap the label? Like, it could be a child of the label, anchored to right center. Then it could be also hidden with visibility instead of modulate.

That might work, I'll give it a spin.
Update: doesn't work

@Mickeon @Calinou @KoBeWi 

After some testing, it seems the remove button will have to be removed from this PR, leaving only the add button, which is fine in my opinion as it saves one click, but also some time to traverse from the project to the Manage Tags button. The removal of the remove button however, will hamper all updates I had planned that relied on this feature and I won't feel good about having an incomplete implementation merged (if it's even possible to get merged with only the add button), so I'll be closing this PR. Thanks for all of the reviews and feedback, it's been very helpful to getting this feature to an approvable state and I have learned lessons that will benefit any and all future PRs of mine.
